functions.name: core_usb_init
functions.brief: Initialize USB CDC. Device appears as /dev/tty.usbmodem* on the host.

functions.name: core_usb_connected
functions.brief: Returns 1 if a host terminal is connected (DTR set).

functions.name: core_usb_wait_host
functions.brief: Wait up to `timeout_ms` for a host terminal to open the port (DTR set). Feeds the watchdog while it waits. Not needed just to see early output: on Core.ST.L4 text printed before the port opens is kept (up to HAL_USB_CDC_TX_QUEUE_SIZE bytes) and sent when it does.

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: Longest wait in milliseconds; 0 only checks.

functions.name: core_usb_write
functions.brief: Transmit data: queued, never waits long (see hal_usb_cdc_write); returns bytes queued, -1 before init.

functions.name: core_usb_try_write
functions.brief: Transmit without waiting: queues the whole buffer or none of it. Returns len if queued, 0 if there is no room right now (offer it again later), -1 if no terminal is connected. Main loop only.

functions.name: core_usb_print
functions.brief: Print a string followed by a newline. Thin wrapper for DSL-style callers.

functions.name: core_usb_print_int
functions.brief: Print a signed integer followed by a newline.

functions.name: core_usb_print_float
functions.brief: Print a double with a newline. %g trims trailing zeros for readability.

functions.name: core_usb_print_bool
functions.brief: Print "true" / "false" followed by a newline.

functions.name: core_usb_on_receive
functions.brief: Set a callback for received data. Called from USB ISR. When set, data is NOT buffered for polling reads.

params.name: cb
params.description: Callback: void cb(const uint8_t *data, uint16_t len, void *ctx)

params.name: ctx
params.description: User context passed to callback; may be NULL

functions.name: core_usb_available
functions.brief: Returns the number of bytes available to read (ring buffer mode).

functions.name: core_usb_getc
functions.brief: Read a single byte (blocking — waits for data).

functions.name: core_usb_read
functions.brief: Read available bytes into buf (non-blocking). Returns bytes read.

functions.name: core_usb_try_read
functions.brief: Non-blocking single byte read. Returns 1 if a byte was read, 0 if empty.

functions.name: core_usb_hid_send
functions.brief: Send a HID report (up to 64 bytes, zero-padded automatically). Blocking — waits for the previous report to be read by the host. Returns bytes of user data sent, or -1 if USB not configured.

functions.name: core_usb_hid_set_rx_callback
functions.brief: Register a callback for inbound HID reports (host -> device). Fires from the USB ISR with one report per call (up to 64 bytes), delivered via the EP3 OUT interrupt endpoint or HID SET_REPORT. Pass NULL to disable; unhandled reports are dropped.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_init
functions.brief: Initialize USB CDC. This function: - Enables HSI48 + CRS (crystal-less 48MHz for USB) - Selects HSI48 as USB clock source - Enables VDDUSB power supply - Configures PA11/PA12 as AF10 - Enables USB peripheral clock - Configures USB device and endpoints - Enables USB interrupt - Connects DP pull-up (host sees device) core_init() already calls it; later calls do nothing.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_connected
functions.brief: Check if the host has opened the virtual COM port. Returns 1 if configured and DTR is set (terminal connected).

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_write
functions.brief: Transmit data over USB CDC. Queues into the TX FIFO (HAL_USB_CDC_TX_QUEUE_SIZE) and returns once the bytes are queued. Before a terminal opens the port (DTR) the bytes wait in the FIFO and go out when it does; what doesn't fit is dropped (the oldest text is kept). With a terminal that isn't reading, it waits at most HAL_USB_CDC_TX_TIMEOUT_MS, then drops. Never waits in an interrupt handler. Returns the number of bytes queued (short = the rest was dropped), or -1 before hal_usb_cdc_init(). (Core.ST.H5 until 2026-09-26: blocking, and -1 with no terminal.)

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_printf
functions.brief: Printf over USB CDC (blocking). Returns number of characters written (from vsnprintf).

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_set_rx_callback
functions.brief: Set a callback for received data. Called from the USB ISR with a pointer to data copied from PMA. If set, data is NOT stored in the ring buffer. If not set, data goes into the ring buffer for polling reads.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_rx_ready
functions.brief: Check if data is available to read (ring buffer mode).

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_getc
functions.brief: Read a single byte (blocking — waits for data).

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_rx_try
functions.brief: Try to read a byte without blocking. Returns 1 if a byte was read, 0 if no data available.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_read
functions.brief: Read available bytes into buffer (non-blocking). Returns number of bytes actually read.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_available
functions.brief: Number of bytes available in the RX buffer.

functions.name: hal_usb_cdc_poll
functions.brief: Poll USB events (call from main loop). Use this as an alternative to interrupt-driven operation.

functions.name: hal_usb_hid_send_report
functions.brief: Send a HID report (up to 64 bytes) via EP3 interrupt IN. Waits for the previous report to complete (at most HAL_USB_HID_TX_TIMEOUT_MS, never in an interrupt handler or while the bus is suspended; a report that can't go is dropped). Returns bytes sent, or -1 if not configured or dropped.

functions.name: hal_usb_hid_set_rx_callback
functions.brief: Set a callback for HID OUT reports (host -> device). Called from the USB ISR with one report per call, copied from PMA. Reception arrives via the EP3 OUT interrupt endpoint and via the HID SET_REPORT control request. If no callback is set, OUT reports are dropped (the endpoint is still re-armed).

functions.name: ll_usb_power_on
functions.brief: Power-on and reset the USB peripheral. Call after enabling the USB clock (ll_rcc_apb1_clk_enable(LL_APB1_USB)).

functions.name: ll_usb_connect
functions.brief: Enable the DP pull-up resistor (signals device connection to host).

functions.name: ll_usb_disconnect
functions.brief: Disable the DP pull-up (disconnect from host).

functions.name: ll_usb_set_address
functions.brief: Set the USB device address and enable function.

functions.name: ll_usb_ep_config
functions.signature: ll_usb_ep_config(uint8_t ep, uint16_t type, uint8_t addr)
functions.brief: Configure an endpoint: type and address, EP_KIND clear, both data toggles DATA0 and both directions NAK, in one write. A USB reset already zeroes the toggles; SET_CONFIGURATION without one does not, and RM0394 §46.6.2 makes initializing DTOG mandatory for non-control endpoints. Stale CTR flags are cleared (written 0).

functions.name: ll_usb_pma_write
functions.signature: ll_usb_pma_write(uint16_t pma_offset, const uint8_t * buf, uint16_t len)
functions.brief: Copy data from user buffer to PMA. pma_offset: byte offset in PMA (must be even) buf:        source data len:        number of bytes to copy

functions.name: ll_usb_pma_read
functions.signature: ll_usb_pma_read(uint16_t pma_offset, uint8_t * buf, uint16_t len)
functions.brief: Copy data from PMA to user buffer.

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_power_on
functions.brief: Power-on and reset the USB peripheral. Call after enabling the USB clock.

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_connect
functions.brief: Enable the DP pull-up resistor (signals device connection to host).

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_disconnect
functions.brief: Disable the DP pull-up (disconnect from host).

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_set_address
functions.brief: Set the USB device address and enable function.

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_chep_config
functions.signature: ll_usb_drd_chep_config(uint8_t ep, uint32_t type, uint8_t addr)
functions.brief: Configure an endpoint: type and address, EPKIND clear, both data toggles DATA0 and both directions NAK, in one write; stale VTRX/VTTX are cleared (written 0) and the host-mode upper half is written 0. A USB reset zeroes the toggles, SET_CONFIGURATION without one does not, and RM0481 §55.6.7 makes initializing DTOG mandatory for non-control endpoints. (This used to leave the toggles as they were: a re-configure, or an app started after the ROM bootloader, could lose the first packet as a "duplicate".)

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_pma_write
functions.signature: ll_usb_drd_pma_write(uint32_t pma_offset, const uint8_t * buf, uint16_t len)
functions.brief: Copy data from user buffer to PMA. pma_offset: byte offset in PMA (should be 4-byte aligned) buf:        source data len:        number of bytes to copy

functions.name: ll_usb_drd_pma_read
functions.signature: ll_usb_drd_pma_read(uint32_t pma_offset, uint8_t * buf, uint16_t len)
functions.brief: Copy data from PMA to user buffer.
